scope_statement: A plural, independent MAS tradition study spanning distributed problem solving, formal/public communication, task and team coordination, strategic interaction, organisations/norms, distributed reasoning, learning, robustness and contemporary human/LLM-agent translation. Completeness is bounded to the examined domain families and 76 registered candidate claims, not all publications or a claim of field-wide consensus.
scope_boundaries: No requester repositories, runtime designs, earlier Evolved packets or sibling corpora were consulted. Static prompt provenance is not evidence.
Distributed systems results enter only where a MAS source explicitly uses or motivates them; there is no general distributed-systems audit or blanket Byzantine terminology.
Robotics/control, AI logic, economics and organisational engineering are examined at documented MAS intersections, not as independently complete sibling traditions.
No catalogue of current software products, all FIPA implementations, all voting/mechanism variants, every MARL algorithm or every AAMAS paper is claimed.
Current evidence includes selected 2025–2026 research, current-year source discovery and version verification through the cut-off; proceedings indexing is not paper-level inspection.
LLM results are not the definition of MAS. Formal model properties, simulated behaviour, field trials, implementation and causal benefit are kept distinct.
An examined unresolved access/version question is not silently recast as disproof; selected whole-system transfer remains unvalidated.

candidate_boundary_rationale: Candidates were split when triggers, mechanisms or assumptions differ (for example task completion versus collective outcome; generic fault modelling versus replicated DCOP; norm enforcement versus norm-aware planning). Synonyms were not multiplied. Late sources added EMAS-075/076, while the human-explanation null result revised existing EMAS-028/068. No fixed property count was used as a discovery ceiling. Final argument-dialogue sources refined the existing reasoning criterion and its protocol/termination coupling, rather than creating a property for each published protocol.

saturation_rationale.STANDARD: Decision-relevant saturation inside the declared scope, not bibliographic exhaustiveness or a time/source quota.
saturation_rationale.EVIDENCE: Each mandatory family has inspected founding or authoritative formulations, an operative mechanism, critical/limiting evidence, a contemporary connection and a candidate/composition disposition. Current searches changed the denominator and weakened convenient pro- and anti-MAS narratives before closure.
saturation_rationale.STOPPING_JUDGEMENT: Further repeated discovery themes were producing alternative examples of already represented mechanisms, not a new identified property, changed prerequisite or missing mandatory branch. Specific inaccessible versions and wider field transfer remain explicitly examined limits rather than invented closure.
REOPEN_CONDITIONS: Readable final/current FIPA profiles and conformance evidence
A materially different failure or protocol model
Independent comparative field evidence that changes configuration selection
A counterexample to a retained formal/analytical claim
Evidence that a genealogy edge reflects derivation rather than shared ancestry or analogy
saturation_rationale.UNCERTAINTY: Saturation is the researcher’s bounded coverage judgement; it is not a proof that no omitted publication could change a conclusion.

uncompleted_burdens_explanation: No registered candidate or mandatory family remains NOT_EXAMINED. Unresolved version/evidence/transfer questions are retained above and in the composition model, not represented as unfinished reading.

nodes.PROBLEM: Strategic reports and incompatible allocative desiderata.
nodes.MECHANISM: Restricted mechanism/choice models with explicit impossibility results.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Results imported into MAS reasoning, not invented by MAS.
nodes.LIMITS: Different domain, participation or randomisation assumptions change applicability.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Systematic treatment in the inspected MAS foundations manuscript; native allocation work requires additional engineering assumptions.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Distributed problem solving and Contract Net
nodes.PROBLEM: Loosely coupled processors must find suitable recipients for distributed tasks and share results.
nodes.MECHANISM: Task announcements, bids, awards; task-sharing/result-sharing distinction.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A canonical high-level distributed control protocol and decomposition vocabulary.
nodes.LIMITS: Not proof of task completion, truthful reporting or universal optimality. The 1977 predecessor is mentioned but not independently read.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Later marginal-cost and contract-type work changes allocative mechanisms; not a single linear replacement.

nodes.PROBLEM: Concurrent local plans interact under incomplete information.
nodes.MECHANISM: Selected local plans, partial global views and continuing activity coordination.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Interleaves planning, communication and execution rather than requiring one complete prior plan.
nodes.LIMITS: Original meta-organisation and vehicle-monitoring simulation constrain generality; stale plans can cause failures.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Its explicit coordination costs remain relevant to later teamwork and modern multi-agent claims; direct influence is not inferred solely from similar terms.

nodes.PROBLEM: What agents can know jointly with uncertain communication.
nodes.MECHANISM: Epistemic models distinguish shared knowledge levels and their attainable conditions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: A formal boundary on idealised coordination requirements.
nodes.LIMITS: Not a theorem against all cooperation or all asynchronous protocols.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Helps discriminate ideal semantics from practical notification requirements; does not replace teamwork theories.

nodes.PROBLEM: Parallel intentions do not explain persistence and repair of a joint undertaking.
nodes.MECHANISM: Joint persistent goals; commitment and reconsideration/notification conventions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Joint activity includes duties about changed feasibility and goal status.
nodes.LIMITS: Ideal mental-state assumptions; centrality is a school’s thesis, not field consensus.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: STEAM operationalises selected ideas; social-commitment work chooses a different public semantic object.

nodes.PROBLEM: A team can act before recipes and allocations are fully settled.
nodes.MECHANISM: Partial shared plans, intentions towards others and reconciliation.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Represents incomplete collaborative planning without collapsing it into one aggregate intention.
nodes.LIMITS: Does not by itself provide continuous monitoring of external action.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Explicitly drawn upon, alongside joint intentions, in STEAM; remains an alternative explanatory account.

nodes.PROBLEM: Formal teamwork must be operational and communication has a cost.
nodes.MECHANISM: Team monitoring/repair, selective communication and decision-theoretic analysis.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Turns team commitments into action-relevant monitoring and notification choices.
nodes.LIMITS: Simulation/application programmes and finite decision models do not establish universal superiority.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Refines rather than eliminates the theoretical distinction between intention, communication and observed success.

nodes.PROBLEM: Heterogeneous agents need a language/protocol for knowledge and action requests.
nodes.MECHANISM: Performatives, content separation and specified communicative-act semantics.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Makes communication layers and intended effects explicit.
nodes.LIMITS: The inspected FIPA specimen is experimental XC00037H dated 2001-08-10, not the inaccessible later final texts.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Singh’s critique disputes private mental-state foundations for open systems; standardisation does not settle the dispute.

nodes.PROBLEM: Opaque agents cannot publicly verify one another’s private beliefs.
nodes.MECHANISM: Social obligations and lifecycle rules; alignment under specified transport and local-observation conditions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Public interaction can be specified without assuming shared implementation internals.
nodes.LIMITS: Alignment at quiescence under the paper’s assumptions is neither instant omniscience nor fulfilled external work.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Continues a distinct social-semantic approach; not a universally stronger replacement for inspectable mental-state models.

nodes.PROBLEM: Rigid control-flow descriptions poorly capture distributed enactment.
nodes.MECHANISM: Information causality, keys/bindings and legal local message steps.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Permits flexible interaction while analysing enactability and model-level completion possibility.
nodes.LIMITS: Protocol liveness has a precise weaker meaning than eventual work completion; later implementation is short-form evidence.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: The 2025 SARL work explicitly translates the BSPL mechanism into an implementation environment.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Economic task exchange and contract structures
nodes.PROBLEM: Task bundles, costs and incomplete deliberation complicate naive bidding.
nodes.MECHANISM: Marginal-cost exchange; decommitment and richer contract neighbourhoods.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Bridges distributed control with economic and bounded-rational decision assumptions.
nodes.LIMITS: Cost/pricing regimes do not automatically establish honesty, social welfare or arbitrary resource externalities.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Preserves several branches: central allocation, cooperative estimates, strategic mechanisms and limited search.

nodes.PROBLEM: Analysis and design need roles, permissions and interaction responsibilities.
nodes.MECHANISM: Role/protocol models and documented adaptation of object-oriented methodological ideas.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Documents an intersection of MAS organisational concepts with agent-oriented engineering.
nodes.LIMITS: Original scope restricts changing abilities/services and open strategic participation.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Useful genealogy for a later AOSE comparison, not a substitute for independently studying that tradition.

nodes.PROBLEM: Organisation must connect structural roles to goals and obligations, and sometimes change.
nodes.MECHANISM: Structural, functional and deontic models; monitored design/select/implement revision.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Makes different organisational dimensions and revision responsibilities explicit.
nodes.LIMITS: Early examples are simulated; reorganisation cannot repair every failed goal or environment.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Later normative and plan-integration work addresses enforcement and operational gaps without proving general self-government.

nodes.PROBLEM: A declared obligation can be violated and the event may not be observable.
nodes.MECHANISM: Institutional state, norm monitoring, prevention, sanctions and grievance-based handling.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Separates normative specification from enforceable operational effects.
nodes.LIMITS: Formal guarantees assume observable/modelled actions; computational authority is not external jurisdiction.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Norm-aware BDI is a different 2026 branch: planning with norms rather than merely imposing controls.

nodes.PROBLEM: Distributed agents must choose consistent or low-cost assignments.
nodes.MECHANISM: Asynchronous search, bounds, pseudo-tree dynamic programming and privacy-preserving protocol variants.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Provides precise feasibility/quality/computation trade-offs.
nodes.LIMITS: Transport, graph width, leakage and model correctness constrain guarantees.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: A 2026 fault-tolerant extension addresses a specific corruption model; it is not generic consensus.

nodes.PROBLEM: Conflicting arguments require semantics for acceptability.
nodes.MECHANISM: Argument/attack structures and admissible, preferred, stable and grounded semantics.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: AI/non-monotonic-logic contribution reused in MAS deliberation.
nodes.LIMITS: Graph acceptance does not independently warrant the truth of premises; some semantics can have no extension.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: A documented interdisciplinary import, not evidence that all social agreement is factual knowledge.

nodes.PROBLEM: A plural field needs a systematic conceptual and mathematical account.
nodes.MECHANISM: Distributed problem solving, strategic games, social choice and mechanism design presented with distinct assumptions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Documents the coexistence of computational and economic approaches.
nodes.LIMITS: The inspected revision is an uncorrected manuscript, not every later corrected edition.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: A taxonomy/definition source; original theorems were sought separately for load-bearing impossibility claims.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Deep MARL, CTDE, factorisation and Other-Play
nodes.PROBLEM: Learning agents face non-stationarity, credit assignment and conventions that do not transfer.
nodes.MECHANISM: Centralised training/local execution, monotonic value mixing, symmetry-based cross-play preparation.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Makes learning and partner dependence explicit operational design objects.
nodes.LIMITS: Controlled games, representation classes and known symmetries limit claims.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: 2025 benchmarking and 2026 coordination environments test generalisation and cost without establishing universal open-world competence.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Strategic decision aids and human-agent collectives
nodes.PROBLEM: People and algorithms must combine recommendations, information and real action.
nodes.MECHANISM: Human-constrained security schedules; mixed-initiative task assignment and participant control.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Shows different forms of applied MAS and external participation.
nodes.LIMITS: An airport deployment report and staged disaster trials are different evidence kinds; neither proves the full field’s causal effectiveness.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Current human-agent experiments ask when explanations aid collaboration; human involvement is not automatically useful or ceremonial.

nodes.PROBLEM: Participants can rebuild good reputation and then defect again.
nodes.MECHANISM: Explicit con-man histories and modified direct-trust dynamics.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Negative evidence against unqualified reputation-based safety.
nodes.LIMITS: Simplified two-agent histories; first defection is not prevented.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Supports bounded exposure and threat-specific evidence, not elimination of trust as a useful heuristic.

nodes.PROBLEM: Language agents can exchange reasoning but incur costs and coupled failures.
nodes.MECHANISM: Debate, trace analysis, equal-budget comparisons and long-horizon coordination benchmarks.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Positive component evidence and increasingly discriminating negative comparisons.
nodes.LIMITS: Shared sources, judges, models and unmatched training/inference budgets restrict independence and generality.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Retain actual mechanisms; neither a universal MAS benefit nor universal single-agent superiority is warranted.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Norm formation, collusion and specialist bottlenecks
nodes.PROBLEM: Stable cooperation, strategic adaptation and specialisation can have adverse collective effects.
nodes.MECHANISM: Controlled common-pool norms, finite pricing meta-games and kitchen collaboration simulation.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Recent tests differentiate behavioural stability from social value and expose coordination costs.
nodes.LIMITS: Simulated populations, finite strategies and short-form reports limit transfer.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Requires explicit normative criteria and task-specific alternatives rather than a progress narrative.

nodes.PROBLEM: Existing mechanisms need robustness or normative action integration.
nodes.MECHANISM: Replicated Max-Sum messages under a fault/knowledge model; norm-related plan alternatives.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Two specific extensions with different objects and guarantees.
nodes.LIMITS: Approximate optimisation remains approximate; running-example norm awareness is not universal compliance.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Retained as domain-specific additions, not compulsory new layers for every MAS.

nodes.PROBLEM: Useful team transparency competes with attention and action speed.
nodes.MECHANISM: Hierarchical policy subtask explanations compared across text/audio/control conditions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Adds a current null result and recipient-specific communication question.
nodes.LIMITS: Small experienced convenience sample and one layout; no significant difference is not equivalence.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: Refines selective communication and human participation rather than creating a universal explanation requirement.

nodes.SCHOOL_OR_WORK: Argumentation-based inter-agent dialogue and protocol critique
nodes.PROBLEM: Agents must exchange and challenge reasons, not merely calculate acceptability privately.
nodes.MECHANISM: Preference-sensitive argument generation plus dialogue moves, public stores and private rationality preconditions.
nodes.CONTRIBUTION: Documents an explicit Dung-inspired MAS adaptation and a criticism-led distinction between trace legality, private conformance and termination.
nodes.LIMITS: Basic model is two-party, omits retraction and relies on relevance/useful-stopping assumptions; it is not a general negotiation or truth guarantee.
nodes.RECEPTION_OR_LATER_RELATION: The 2002 analysis distinguishes commitment meanings and the open protocol-design obligations. No current-day research frontier is inferred from its historical claims.

prefreeze_revision_log: All changes occurred before first freeze EMAS-R1; there was no earlier frozen packet whose judgements were silently changed.

Verified/corrected source dates, author lists, exact titles and experimental-versus-final FIPA identity from readable primary covers/text; DOI/deposit/file-name dates were not substituted for publication dates.
Added distinct candidates EMAS-075/076 after current primary research; retained all earlier IDs and unfavourable candidates.
Added EMAS-S054 and refined existing communication/human-participation candidates; did not manufacture a new candidate for an already represented trigger.
Classified Dung argumentation as an interdisciplinary import; retained strictness criticism EMAS-K018 as researcher analysis, not a published correction.
Machine serialisation uses UTF-8, two-space JSON indentation and final newline. Such syntax normalisation does not change the frozen substantive judgement.

A final genealogy check found no support for the draft Dung-to-foundations-manuscript edge. Read EMAS-S055/056 and replaced that edge with the express 2000 MAS dialogue adaptation. Refined EMAS-046, criticism EMAS-K013 and new relation EMAS-REL-061; the complete candidate denominator remains 76 because this is the operating-method coupling of an already registered criterion, not a distinct universally prescribed control.

Final primary-cover check completed the EMAS-S043 author list and December 2016 date; tightened the EMAS-075 fault-model wording to synchronous message passing. Normalised the staged-field-trial evidence-role label without altering its evidence status.

Final adjudication made every evolution transition’s historical-versus-analytical status explicit, so tested overgeneralisations are not falsely attributed to original authors. Export fields with no dedicated pairwise alternative edge received a reasoned absence note. A verification false positive inside the legitimate DOI JZVR6522 was corrected by matching whole target-code tokens, not by changing the citation.
